title: Vernetzte Schweiz 1860–1914
tagline: Address books · Telephone directories · Authority data
lead: Address books of Swiss towns and the early PTT telephone directories, linked to one another and to Wikidata, the Historical Dictionary of Switzerland (HLS) and the Integrated Authority File (GND).
sources_p: Each town is processed in its own repo and taken over here at a pinned version. Authority data are shown down to the «possible» tier; links that the check against the HLS article found to be wrong remain hidden, as do «possible» links with no tie to the town (name and dates only).
phone_p: Entries per canton and year, by the resolved place of each entry. Up to 1910, directories newly processed entry by entry (batch A); 1911–1914, the nationwide volumes (batch B). «–»: place not resolved.

footer_sources: Sources: address books of Aarau (Kantonsbibliothek Aargau), Basel (Staatsarchiv Basel-Stadt), Baden, Bern, Lausanne and Zurich (read with qwen3.8); telephone directories PTT Archive P-260, processed by DH Bern and localsearch (historic.localsearch.ch).

quality_p: In the 1911–1914 volumes the place is given as a heading, which was carried over to the following lines during reading. If a heading is missed, whole pages inherit the wrong place – Zurich 1912 appears as «Zwillikon (Affoltern a. A.)». Such runs are checked against the other years: the same subscribers usually appear in the book for several years.
quality_recovered: entries re-placed by matching across years
kpi_linked: directory entries with an address book entry
links_p: A telephone directory entry is linked to the entries of the same person or firm in each address book volume of the town: same surname, then first name or initial, alliance name, street and house number, occupation and the telephone mark in the address book. A link is made only if exactly one person fits best; if first names or alliance names contradict each other, none is made. The larger the gap in years, the more evidence is required – sons and successors carry on name, house and business.
links_gap: Basel has only the 1862 volume, 19 to 52 years before the telephone directories: there the name alone almost never suffices, and the «certain» tier is not assigned.
links_recall: Recall, measured in Aarau on the entries that carry the telephone mark in the address book and whose surname occurs in the telephone directory within ± 2 years:
links_recall_item: Volume {vol}: {linked} of {reachable} linked ({pct}; {flagged} with telephone mark in total).
ent_h: Persons and firms across the years
ent_p: Entries for the same person or firm are grouped into one entity across telephone directory editions and address book volumes, per municipality. Evidence is the same number, first name, address, occupation and the pairs from the address book linking. If first names or alliance names contradict each other, or if a widow and her husband, or a business and its successors, appear side by side, no grouping is made. The entities then receive authority data: taken over from the towns, otherwise via Wikidata and the municipality number.
ent_multi: Entities with more than one entry
ent_quality_note: Assessed by Claude against the printed text, not by the project staff. With 10–30 cases per layer, one case shifts the figure by 3–10 points.
auth_note: New links, checked against the directory entry and Wikidata (occupation, dates, places): «probable» {p} correct (n = {n}), «possible» {p2} (n = {n2}). Links are made via Wikidata and the FSO municipality number, never via the bare name.
auth_note_none: Links are made via Wikidata and the FSO municipality number, never via the bare name.
pg_search_p: The search covers the surname or firm name, from the beginning, ignoring accents: «Muller» finds «Müller». Further words narrow it down by first name (also in another language form: «Charles» finds «Carl»), occupation or addition; the second field by municipality. «Similar names» finds spelling variants and misreadings. A municipality alone (no name) lists everyone if it has fewer than 50 people and firms.
pg_search_ph: Surname or firm name, e.g. Burckhardt Carl
pg_search_hint: Enter at least two letters of the name.
pg_place_big: {p} has {n} people and firms, too many to list them all. Enter a name (at least two letters).
pg_hits_more: The first 300 are shown; first name or municipality narrow it down.
pg_auth_ptt: Matched via Wikidata and the municipality number.
pg_auth_note: «Probable» and «possible» are suggestions, not certainties. Whether the person in the directory is the person in Wikidata can only be shown by comparison with the sources.
pg_timeline_label: Years in which the entity appears in the directory or address book
pg_maybe_p: Address book entries that the linking with the telephone directory (M2) suggests as possible, but which are not grouped into this entity.
pg_map_note: The dot marks the municipality (1914), not the address.
pg_map_error: The map could not be loaded.
pg_address_p: All entries with this street and house number, across all years. Numbers change with renumbering; in Aarau, old town-wide building numbers and new street numbers run side by side.
pg_place_entities: {p} persons, {f} firms and offices (directory and address book)
pg_place_years_p: Only editions that survive; missing years do not mean there were no subscribers.
pg_place_top_p: Persons (entities from directory and address book) are counted, not entries.
pg_places_p: Municipalities (1914) with directory entries, by number of entries.
pg_caveats: Telephone directories and address books were read and parsed by text recognition and language models. Names, numbers and addresses may be misread; the printed book is authoritative. Each entry gives its reference.

The telephone directory shows subscribers, not the population. Up to 1914 it was mainly firms, offices, doctors, inns and well-off households that had a telephone. Missing years mean missing editions, not missing connections.
The place of a directory entry is inferred from headings and exchanges (M1). Only entries with a certain or probable place are grouped and shown. The map dot marks the municipality, not the address.

Telephone directory and address book are linked in three tiers (certain, probable, possible). Measured on assessed samples, 80–100 % are correct depending on town and tier; the larger the gap in years, the less reliable.

Entries are grouped per municipality into the same person or firm. Father and son with the same name, widows and successors are separated where the entries show it; where not, they may be confused. If someone moves to another municipality, two entities result. Of the entries that reappear in the next edition, 75–92 % are measured to be linked there; the rest form an entity of their own.

Wikidata, HLS and GND links are «probable» (name, place and occupation match) or «possible». The towns matched their address book entries themselves and in part checked them against the HLS article. Rejected suggestions are not shown.

The samples from which the percentages derive were assessed by Claude (a language model) against the printed text, not by the project staff. The assessed cases, with reasons, are in the repo (data/review/).

Code and site are under the MIT licence. The contents of the telephone directories and address books up to 1914 are in the public domain: under the Copyright Act, directories arranged by alphabetical or geographical criteria generally lack originality (Art. 2 para. 1 URG), and where a work did exist, the term of protection has expired (Art. 29 para. 2 URG). Data and links are released under CC0 and may be freely reused. From the HLS we take only facts, no article text.
Baden, Bern, Lausanne, Zurich: not post-corrected

The address books of Baden (1900, 1910), Bern (1883–84, 1900), Lausanne (1896, 1907) and Zurich (1867, 1875, 1885, 1900, 1914) were read by the language model qwen3.8 without manual correction; in samples, 83–84 % of entries were fully correct in Bern, 93–96 % in Baden, and all 30 checked in Lausanne. The Baden 1910 scan lacks leaves (town of Baden from «Rü…», Bellikon, Bergdietikon up to «P»); the volume covers the whole district, and each entry counts for its municipality. In Bern, where many namesakes live in the same town, the rules are stricter: abbreviated streets («Kramg.») count as a street match, an initial plus the telephone mark is no longer enough for common surnames, and generic firm words («Schweizerische», «Café», «Bureau») need the same street. After this, 32 of 40 checked links were correct, 4 unclear and 4 wrong; «certain» 10 of 10. The 1907 Indicateur vaudois also covers the other Vaud communes; each entry's commune is taken from the heading in the book. In the Montreux district only entries naming a locality (Clarens, Territet …) are included. In Zurich the suburbs of 1875 and 1885 (Aussersihl, Riesbach …) count as the city; in the 1914 volume the last entries are missing on 11 pages. Of 30 Zurich links checked (1914), 27 were right, «certain» and «probable» 10 of 10 each.
pg_entries_merged: Identical lines from several editions of the same year are merged: {n} lines.
pg_occ_p: The search covers the occupation field of the entries, from the start of a word, ignoring accents: «Uhrmach» finds «Uhrmacher» and «Uhrmacherei». The directories are in German, French and Italian; with «Include translations», «Metzger» also finds «boucher». A second word narrows it down («fabr horlog»). The slider selects years: results attested within that range.
pg_occ_hint: Enter at least three letters of an occupation.
pg_occ_map_note: Circle area = number of results in the municipality. Entities are counted, not entries; the dot is the municipality, not the address.
mp_telefon_p: Each person and each firm counts once, in the first year in which it appears in the directory. The slider selects a year or a range (drag both handles); clicking a bar selects a year. Filter by type, occupational class and canton.
mp_telefon_note: Read with care: the first year is the first surviving edition, not the year of connection. Up to 1910 only individual editions survive (batch A); 1911–1914, the whole of Switzerland annually (batch B). The jump in 1911 comes from this, not from a boom. The number of municipalities with entries in the selected range is shown below the map. This map counts the telephone directory only.
mp_berufe_p: Where were which occupations? «Count» shows the persons and firms of the class as a heatmap, «Share» the share of all entities in the municipality (only municipalities with at least 20), so that Zurich and Basel do not fill every map. Counted are those in the selected source within the selected range; the address books cover only Aarau (1867–1899) and Basel (1862).
mp_berufe_note: Occupational classes from keywords (medicine, hospitality, watches …). Measured on 60 random entities, 88–92 % are correctly classified; but around 40 % of entities have no class, and some of these list an occupation the keywords do not know. For a specific occupation: the occupation search.
mp_namen_p: Clicking a municipality shows the five most frequent surnames in the selected range and source. A name in the search field shows where persons of that name appear within the range, and the centre of gravity per year (red line, dots within the range larger).
mp_namen_note: The centre of gravity also moves because editions are missing or added: in 1911 the whole of Switzerland is added. A person counts for every year between their first and last entry, even if an edition in between is missing. Same name does not mean same family. Address books exist only for Aarau and Basel.

ft_p: Searches all 638 701 telephone directory entries up to 1914, not the grouped persons: every word must occur, in any field or in the selected one. «Exact» finds the word, «approximate» also spelling variants and misreadings («Mttler» → «Müller»). Results by year, oldest first.

ft_fields_note: The fields come from parsing the lines and are not always separated correctly (occupation in the street, first name in the name); if a field finds nothing, try the general search field.

hl_h: From the HLS to the entry
hl_intro: Which persons in the Historical Dictionary of Switzerland (HLS) ought to appear in the telephone directories and address books of 1880–1914, and where do we find them? Expected are those who were adults in these years and lived or died in a place for which a book survives for these years.
hl_sum: {e} HLS persons expected; {s} found (authority data or probable), plus {c} with candidates to check.
hl_sum_note: Weighted by the measured hit rates, this is around 26 %. Many of those missing had no telephone or did not live at their place of death.
hl_s_text: place with year from the article
hl_s_long_text: The places come from statements with a year in the HLS article, plus the place of death.
hl_s_long_gelebt: The places come from Wikidata (residence or place of work), plus the place of death.
hl_s_long_nur_sterbeort: Only the place of death is known; it does not reliably say where the person lived in 1880–1914.
hl_cell_nobook: at this place, but no book for the year
hl_cell_out: outside the years at this place
hl_cands_p: Entities in the place with the same surname, listed in years in which the person was an adult. «Authority data» is a link from M3; all other tiers are suggestions.
hl_r_name_fehlt: The surname does not occur in our data, not even elsewhere. A misreading in the telephone directory is possible.
hl_r_name_nicht_am_ort: The surname occurs, but not in this person's places during their years.
hl_r_name_ohne_vorname: The surname appears in the place, but with a different first name or in other years.
hl_r_name_anderswo: Someone with the same surname and first name appears in another place (below). Perhaps the person lived there, perhaps it is a namesake.
hl_far_p: Entities with the same surname and a matching first name in other places, in years in which the person was an adult.
hl_why_text: place and year from the article
hl_note: From the HLS we take only name, dates and the number; the article can be read at hls-dhs-dss.ch.
hl_hint_note: Suggestion from the reverse check (same surname, first name and occupation in the place), not authority data.
city_no_authority: Machine-read volumes bring no authority data from the source repo; Wikidata and HLS are linked via the persons.
meta_description: Address books of Swiss towns and early PTT telephone directories, linked to Wikidata, the HLS and the GND.
mw_p: Who disappears from one place and shortly afterwards appears for the first time in another? Same surname, compatible written-out forename, at most 6 years in between; the more that agrees (same occupation, title, rare name), the higher the tier. Only pairs that are unique in both directions count. Lines lead from the old to the new place (red dot); «Balance» shows arrivals and departures per place (green more arrivals, red more departures).
mw_note: Experimental: candidates, not verified moves. The phone books list subscribers only; «new in the book» often means «new telephone». Before 1911 only single editions exist, so cases cluster in 1911–1914. Pairs that are more likely a place-assignment error (same number, same address, street of the old place, neighbouring lines from the old place, alphabetically adjacent place, place or street word of the old entry) are excluded. Measured: strong 75–88 % correct (sample 3, 8 pairs); weak 52–86 % (sample 4); medium 44–91 % (sample 5); pairs admitted as «ambiguous but clearly ahead», medium 24–92 % (sample 6).
mw_seen: Both places covered before and after
mw_count: {n} possible moves, first year at the new place {y}, between {f} pairs of places.
mw_by_year: First year at the new place

pg_tr_none: No occupation in the list is known for this word; only the wording is searched.
pg_occ_doc: How the occupation search works (in German)

Each frame states how certain the link is; it comes from the entity's authority data, from the check against the HLS or from a migration. Wikidata and Swiss elites are queried when the page opens.

zz_p: Who appears in an address book of {c} for the first time, and where did they come from? The building and resident lists give the home town for about 60 % of persons («von Erfurt», «von Küttigen»). Persons are linked from volume to volume (surname, forename, home town, occupation, house); anyone in neither of the two preceding volumes counts as an arrival. The table compares the share from abroad among arrivals with the share among those who stayed.
zz_note: Experimental: «new» can also be a misread name, and anyone missing for two volumes counts as an arrival on return. Sample of 24 arrivals: 11 clearly new, 12 reading errors or not decidable. Aarau renumbered its buildings between 1869 and 1877; house numbers do not count across that change. The home town is the place of citizenship, not necessarily the last residence.
zz_family_tip: The surname (or maiden or alliance name) was already in the previous volume: perhaps a relative, perhaps a namesake.
zz_col_new: of these, surname new to the town
zz_col_area: District not covered in previous volume
zz_p_names: Who appears in an address book of {c} for the first time? Persons are linked from volume to volume (surname, forename, occupation, street and house); anyone in neither of the two preceding volumes counts as an arrival. These volumes give no home town, so there is no origin and no map.
zz_note_names: Experimental: the volumes are 8 to 15 years apart, so «arrival» means «new since the previous volume» and includes sons who get an entry of their own. The volumes were read without correction; a misread name turns someone who stayed into an arrival. 1867 covers almost only the old town: anyone listed in Aussersihl, Riesbach etc. in 1875 does not count as an arrival (column «not covered»). Streets were partly renamed after the 1893 merger, so the address helps little from 1885 to 1900.
zz_share_country: Share of the {n} arrivals from abroad
zz_share_canton: Share of the {n} arrivals from Switzerland
inf_p: What do telephone directories and address books show of infrastructure growth between 1880 and 1914? Three approaches: the telephone network itself (how many subscribers, where, how early), the occupations and businesses tied to railways, post, electricity, gas, water and transport, and further traces such as public call offices, offices and utilities with a line of their own. Points, years and names lead to the directory of that place and year.
inf_series_p: Directory entries per town and year, on a log scale: lines of equal slope mean equal growth rates. A point leads to the town's directory for that year. Select towns:
inf_series_note: For each town and year the most complete volume counts; a year with less than 90 % of the highest so far is treated as partly read and left out, because a network does not shrink in this period. Towns with at least eight years before 1911. From 1911 the figures come from the nationwide volumes instead of the local directory, so a jump there reflects the source rather than the network. An entry is not a line: firms appear under several names, people with a business and a home twice.
inf_home_p: Share of entries with a home line («Wohnung», «Privat», «domicile», «appartement»): the telephone moves from the shop into the home, at first mostly as a second line of business people. Only years with at least 100 entries are shown; below that, single cases decide. The share also depends on how a directory marks homes: a jump between two years is more likely editing than network.
inf_map_p: Every municipality with at least one entry, coloured by the decade in which it first appears in a directory; size follows the 1914 entries. Other layers show municipalities with a public call office, with offices and utilities, with occupations of a group, or with a Station Street, also by first year. Click a circle to open the municipality. On the layer “Entries per 1,000 inhabitants” the size follows the population in 1910.
inf_map_note: Before 1911 only regional directories exist, one to seven networks per year (Basel, Bern, St. Gallen, Zurich, Geneva, Lausanne, Chur, Bellinzona …). The first year is therefore the first year in an available directory, not the year of connection: a place first listed in 1911 may have had a telephone earlier. This mainly affects Vaud and Valais. From 1911 the nationwide volumes cover all of Switzerland, but not every volume is fully read.
inf_cantons_h: Municipalities with a telephone by canton
inf_cantons_note: Municipalities as of 1 January 1914 (FSO); “by” counts every municipality listed in a directory at least once up to that year. Public call offices: «Gemeindestation», «Gemeindesprechstation», «Station communale», «Station publique», «Stazione pubblica». They show where the network reached people without a line of their own. Click a canton to open its map.
inf_occ_p: Who builds and runs the networks? Seven groups by keywords in the occupation (and in the name for firms and offices). Inns named after the station or the post office do not count; railway companies before the 1902 nationalisation (N.O.B., J.-S., S.C.B., J.-B.-L.) do.
inf_ab_h: In the address books: per 1,000 entries
inf_ab_note: Resident and building lists, without the trade directory. Zürich 1867 covers almost only the old town, 1875–1885 also the suburbs; railway jobs therefore jump in 1875 (station and workshops in Aussersihl). With few volumes, a difference reflects the source rather than change.
inf_nat_note: Click a group to show its municipalities on the map. Directories list subscribers only: a power station or a garage with a telephone, not every electrician or driver. To compare the years, only the volumes read in every year from 1911 to 1914 count (1, 2a, 2b, 3); volume 2c with Ticino is missing for 1913 and 1914.
inf_num_h: Telephone numbers: the size of the exchange
inf_num_p: Distinct numbers count connections better than entries do: a firm is listed under several names but with one number. The highest number shows how far the exchange has handed out its numbers. When it jumps while connections grow steadily, the exchange was renumbered: in 1896 Basel goes from at most 2,200 to 4,302, with 2,146 connections; the new exchange is only half occupied.
inf_num_note: Only years in which at least 80% of entries have a legible number. The highest number is the end of the continuous range around the median number; a block after a gap of more than 300 numbers (neighbouring exchange, misreading) does not count. “Occupied” = numbers / highest number.
inf_werk_note: Utilities: counted by the name of a business or office (“Elektrizitätswerk Wangen”, “Usine à gaz”, “Wasserversorgung der Stadt Bern”), not by a person’s occupation; a “Gas-, Wasser- und Elektrizitätswerk” counts three times. A works is listed in the municipality of its line: the Lucerne city electricity works with its power station in Engelberg.
inf_amt_note: Offices: by the name of the entry (“Gemeindekanzlei”, “Greffe municipal”, “Bahnhof”, “Gare”, “Postbureau”, “Telegraphenbureau”); inns such as “Hôtel de la Gare” do not count, nor does a municipal clerk with a line under his own name. “Station communale” and “Stazione pubblica” are public call offices, not railway stations; “Poste de gendarmerie” is a police post, not a post office. The post office was often also the public call office and is therefore listed separately less often.
inf_tour_p: Hotels, spa houses and guesthouses among a place’s entries in the year it first appears in a telephone directory.
inf_tour_list: {n} municipalities where hotels and spa houses make up at least half of the first entries (at least 5); year, hotels / entries:
inf_tour_note: Patterns: hotel, hôtel, Kurhaus, Kuranstalt, pension, albergo, sanatorium. Inns and taverns do not count; every village has them.
inf_pop_p: How widespread was the telephone? In the nationwide volumes 1911–1914 every entry counts, even without a resolved place. “Persons” are entries under a personal name, each person once per place. Their share of households is an upper bound for households with a line of their own: many of these persons are tradesmen, shopkeepers or doctors with the telephone in the business.
inf_pop_tip: {d} entries per 1,000 inhabitants ({e} entries in the best year 1909–1914, {p} inhabitants in 1910)
inf_pop_note: Boundaries of 2000: municipalities that merged by 2000 are added together. Only confidently located entries count; {n} municipalities with more than 250 entries per 1,000 inhabitants are missing from the map because their place assignment is wrong ({x} …). In the nationwide volumes 1911–1914 many places have lost their heading; their entries are recovered through the surnames of the regional directory (Burgdorf under «Büren zum Hof», Olten under «Olsberg»). Where no regional directory allows the comparison, the figure is too low (Vevey, Montreux).
inf_rail_p: Did the telephone follow the railway? Municipalities with a station opened by 1910 and municipalities without, by population in 1910: share with a telephone entry by 1911 and with a public call office by 1914. Stations from Wikidata ({s} with an opening year, in {m} municipalities).
inf_rail_note: Municipalities with a station have a telephone somewhat more often, but most of the difference comes from size. Wikidata gives an opening year for only 728 of 1,811 Swiss stations, so “without” also contains municipalities with a station. A station belongs to the nearest municipality within 3 km. Only municipalities whose territory stayed the same until 2000.
inf_cov_p: Entries and municipalities per year, on a log scale. The red line counts every municipality listed in a directory at least once up to that year.
inf_cov_note: 1891 is missing entirely and 1907 has one network only. The jumps in 1898, 1900 and 1909 come from additional regional directories, the jump in 1911 from the nationwide volumes. The trends on this page therefore count “listed at least once up to the year”: a missing year does not lower them.
inf_occ_tel_h: In a town's telephone directories: per 1,000 entries
inf_occ_tel_p: The same groups among a town's subscribers, year by year since its first directory. A point leads to that year's directory.
inf_occ_tel_note: Per year the volume with the most entries; only years with at least 100 entries. The directory lists subscribers: railways and post appear as offices and businesses, not as people in those occupations.
inf_trend_h: Call offices, offices and utilities on the network
inf_trend_p: Municipalities where, up to the year, the directory lists at least once a public call office, a municipal office, a post or telegraph office, a railway station, an electricity, gas or water works with an entry of its own, or an address on Station Street, on a log scale; in grey, municipalities with a telephone at all. In the table, the share of municipalities with a telephone is given in brackets. Click a kind to show its municipalities on the map.
inf_trend_note: The public call office is a village's most common line: by 1914, two in three municipalities with a telephone have one. Electricity works first appear in 1893 and overtake the older gas and water works before 1900. Before 1911 the figures also grow because directories are added; the share in brackets compensates for that.
inf_city_h: Towns: what is in the directory, and since when
inf_city_p: For the towns with long series, the first year in which the directory lists the town, a public call office, an office or a utility. Each year leads to the entry in the directory.
inf_city_note: No year precedes the town's first directory that has been read. “–” means no entry under that name by 1914; the works may be listed under another name or under the town administration.
inf_du_nat_note: Inhabitants interpolated between the censuses of 1910 and 1920; households = inhabitants / 4.53 persons per household (1910 census). Numbers: distinct numbers per place.
inf_du_city_p: The same calculation for the towns selected above, since their first directory: persons with an entry per 100 households. A point leads to that year's directory.
inf_du_class_p: By size of municipality, around 1910 (per municipality the best-read year from 1909 to 1914). The table shows the median municipality of the class, not the sum.

inf_du_src: Inhabitants: municipality articles of the Historical Dictionary of Switzerland (HLS, CC BY-SA 4.0) for {h} municipalities; for {b} more, among them almost all towns, and for the other census years, the censuses as published by the FSO. Both cite the same censuses: {i} of {c} comparable values are identical. Interpolated between census years. Persons per household by canton: Federal Statistical Bureau, Zeitschrift für schweizerische Statistik 1914, p. 222 (Switzerland 1880: 4.66; 1910: 4.53).
zw_note: Experiment: women linked through their marital status (Miss X → Y-X / née X → widow). Measured: husband → widow and wife → widow mostly confirmed; unmarried → married cannot be checked from the directories.
fw_p: Women changed their name on marriage and are therefore missing from the moves. Here their entries are linked through marital status: unmarried («Miss X») → married («Y-X», «née X») → widow, and from the husband to his widow. Mostly within one place.
fw_measure: Measured (sample of 65 pairs): husband → widow 67–93 %, wife → widow 80–100 % correct; unmarried → married cannot be checked from the directories (almost all unclear), and across municipalities it does not hold.
